q1: How is the fluorine content related to the CF4 concentration in the used plasma?
a1: Based on subfigure a, it is shown that an increase in the CF4 concentration results in more fluorine in the film.
q2: How does the CF4 concentration determine the stoichiometry of the film?
a2: An increase in CF4 concentration seems to induce a shift from more CF3 and C-CFx bonds towards more CF and CF2 bonds.
q3: Can the shift in peak position for fluorine say something about the stoichiometry?
a3: Yes, usually a shift in peak position indicates different stoichiometries. This is proven by the spectrum from carbon where the change in stoichiometry also introduces different peaks.
q4: can it be said that there is more carbon in the film in the case that the CF4 concentration is 3.3% with respect to the 6.6% case?
a4: This conclusion can not be drawn from the bare carbon spectrum. Calculations of atomic composition require more material specific parameters than the pure XPS spectrum.
